decisions.subject: Decision authority for architecture, scope, release readiness, exceptions, and proof-API changes

options.summary: The sponsor alone accepts every decision.
The sponsor plus a named technical owner, who may be the same person, with delegated acceptance of contract records and pre-registrations.

decisions.rationale: Terms of reference §9 already names "Sponsor and technical owner" as the authority for Q2 and Q4; choosing the sponsor alone would require amending that column.

retired_statements.text: Requested the work; final technical and release authority still needs explicit designation.
It does not itself approve a release, set budgets, or resolve the questions above.

decisions.subject: Trusted-boundary exception policy

options.summary: An exception is valid from its approval date until its `invalid_from` date, at most 90 days and never past the next release-gate task (4.3.3 or 6.3.4); renewal is a new approval; an exception names a narrowed claim and can never satisfy a proof-required component.

decisions.rationale: Bounded lifetimes force each exception to be revisited, and a narrowed claim keeps an exception from being read as proof (technical design §17.2, GAP9).

options.summary: Accept the Core, Integration, and Deferred split in technical design §2 unchanged.
Amend the scope matrix in technical design §2 before acceptance.

decisions.rationale: The split already maps every requirement to a roadmap phase and keeps integration work out of the Core acceptance dossier.

retired_statements.text: The classes remain proposed pending ToR Q4.
The **Core** scope is the proposed initial numeric-language release.

decisions.subject: Package licence

options.summary: Ratify the ISC licence already recorded in `Cargo.toml`, `LICENSE`, and `README.md`.

decisions.rationale: Publication before the Core dossier would promise distribution terms for an unproven library.

approval_reference.answer: Accepted. Ensure this is clearly documented in the developer's guide.

decisions.subject: Pre-1.0 API and public proof-interface compatibility policy

options.summary: Ratify ToR C5 and technical design §15 row 10 (no shims for pre-1.0 or unreleased APIs); follow Cargo's 0.y.z rule (a change to the leftmost non-zero component is breaking); version the public proof interface (models, pre- and postconditions, lemmas, trust declarations) with the crate version, treating a strengthened precondition or weakened postcondition as breaking (technical design §17.8). MSRV stays with ToR Q3 and task 1.2.1.

decisions.rationale: It applies the existing no-compatibility-machinery constraint to both the Rust API and the proof interface that downstream proofs depend on.

retired_statements.text: No blanket source-API compatibility machinery is proposed for this unreleased, pre-1.0 library.

decisions.subject: Dispositions of the candidate ADR subjects

options.summary: Numerical and array semantics to ADR-0006; macro staging and stable-Rust application to ADR-0007; initial release scope to ADR-0003; public proof compatibility to ADR-0005 and ADR-0009; shared semantic kernel and backend and cell separation deferred to task 1.2.1 (B01 can falsify the kernel in 1.2.4); resource certification deferred to step 2.4 (B03); backend input and output control scope deferred to task 1.2.6 (B06).

decisions.rationale: Each subject is decided where its evidence arises; subjects that depend on unrun bets are deferred to the tasks that run them.

approval_reference.answer:
Accepted. Please update the documentation style guide to place ADRs in `docs/adrs/` with naming pattern `adr-nnnn-foo-bar-qux.md` where `nnnn` is a four digit index and `foo-bar-qux` is the title slug. Similarly, RFCs in `docs/rfcs/` with naming pattern `rfc-nnnn-foo-bar-qux.md`

This breaks from current DF12 standards, but the current practice is really starting to bug me and I want to take this opportunity to revise it. If it goes well, we will update the centralized documentation style guide in `agent-helper-scripts` documentation library.

decisions.subject: `comb!` operator precedence

options.summary: Rust's expression precedence as parsed by `syn`, with `|>` split from the token stream first (lowest precedence, left-associative); reject, with a first-screen diagnostic, any comparison that is the unparenthesized operand of `&`, `|`, or `^` and vice versa; translate the chained-comparison error from `syn` into the same diagnostic.

decisions.rationale: Reusing Rust precedence keeps `comb!` readable to Rust developers, and rejecting comparison mixed with bitwise operators removes the one precedence trap Rust users commonly misread.

decisions.subject: F64 special values in reductions and binary `min` and `max`

options.summary: Binary `min` and `max` follow IEEE 754-2019 `minimum` and `maximum` (NaN propagates; negative zero is less than positive zero); null propagation takes precedence over NaN; an empty F64 `sum` returns positive zero (the registered typed zero) while `sum([-0.0])` returns negative zero (a singleton passes through); a `mean` count of exactly 2^53 is admitted.

decisions.rationale: IEEE 754-2019 `minimum` and `maximum` are total and deterministic, unlike the NaN-ignoring `minNum` and `maxNum` operations.

retired_statements.text: The proposed binary contract propagates NaN, with signed-zero ties choosing negative zero for min and positive zero for max.

decisions.subject: Typed-cell atomicity

options.summary: Record two distinct rules under distinct names: cell atomicity (a typed cell such as `DVec3` is one logical element until an explicit component operation; `Batch<DVec3>` of shape `[2,3]` has cardinality 6) and atomic output commit (failure or cancellation before commit leaves the destination unchanged).

decisions.rationale: The single phrase "typed-cell atomicity" had been used for two unrelated guarantees.

decisions.subject: Acceptance measurement environments

options.summary: A named, otherwise idle reference machine (CPU model, cores, memory, governor, SMT, kernel, isolation).

Paired, interleaved runs within one hosted job on a pinned `ubuntu-24.04` runner class, with instruction counts as the primary metric and wall time secondary; proof and build ceilings use the same runner class; shared development hosts are never acceptance environments.

decisions.rationale: The hosted paired design needs no dedicated hardware and controls drift by interleaving.

approval_reference.answer: Accepted, although for local development boxes you'll have to take what you're given. Don't leak hostnames into the source documentation.

retired_statements.text: Pre-register proof runtime, solver memory, build latency, runner size, and cache policy under ToR Q2.

options.summary: The sponsor supplies or amends every threshold value in the pre-registration proposal.
Delegate threshold selection to calibration: realistic measurements on the development machine, extrapolated to the hosted runner class, with the evidence recorded.

decisions.rationale: Thresholds govern acceptance, so the planning agent did not choose them itself.

approval_reference.answer: Make realistic measurements on the current machine and extrapolate to a GitHub runner specced above. I'll trust your judgement here, just bring reasonable evidence.

retired_statements.text: Quantitative performance/compile-cost/proof-cost thresholds require resolution of Q2 before any benchmark-dependent acceptance decision.
Budget numbers, supported target matrix, and performance thresholds remain ToR Q2/Q3.
No thresholds or benchmark outcomes currently exist.

decisions.subject: Governance enforcement

options.summary: Commit `.github/CODEOWNERS` naming the D01 logins for the decision, exception, acceptance-control, and semantic-contract registers and the ADRs, with required code-owner review and a required Design contracts check on main.
No `CODEOWNERS` file; the base-revision freeze check and the sponsor's pull request review and merge are the controls, revisited if another developer joins.

decisions.rationale: Code-owner review would make an unauthorized register edit a blocked merge rather than a reviewer catch.

approval_reference.answer: No, we don't do `.github/CODEOWNERS`. If we magically acquire another dev, we can change this.

decisions.subject: `div` on I64 operands

options.summary: Convert each operand to F64 (round to nearest, ties to even), then apply IEEE division, matching Rust `as f64` and common backends; document that this can differ from rounding the exact quotient once.

decisions.rationale: Technical design §6.1 says only "true division to F64"; converting operands first matches what every candidate backend computes.

retired_statements.text: Mixed I64/F64 arithmetic requires an explicit cast except for `div`, which means true division to F64.

decisions.subject: Prospective details for later roadmap tasks

options.summary: Add details to the roadmap now so later criteria are fixed in advance: 1.2.1 and 1.2.4 build the trust-audit scanner and verifier log parsers and replay the gate rule table from Rust; 1.2.3 replays the semantic examples as `rstest` cases; 2.3.1 replays every grammar corpus entry as a `trybuild` pass or fail fixture, with a completeness check.

decisions.rationale: Fixing the replay obligations before those tasks start prevents their success criteria from being chosen after the fact.

approval_reference.answer: Accepted. Note that `docs/roadmap.md` is canonical.
